Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real and distinct roots. If Δ = 0, there is one real root. If Δ < 0, there are no real roots. To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function (f'(x)). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x (f'(x) = 0). The solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. Finally, to determine the nature of the stationary points, find the second derivative (f''(x)) and evaluate it at the x-coordinates of the stationary points. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
